name: MARAG-R1: Beyond Single Retriever via Reinforcement-Learned Multi-Tool Agentic Retrieval
venue: arXiv:2510.27569 (cs.CL); preprint, submitted 31 Oct 2025; no peer-reviewed venue as of retrieval
authors_affiliation: Qi Luo, Xiaonan Li (equal contribution), Yuxin Wang, Tingshuo Fan, Yuan Li, Xinchi Chen, Xipeng Qiu (corresponding); School of Computer Science, Fudan University
code_url: [uncertain] No official code repository found; the paper provides no code link and no MARAG-R1 repo was located via search.
task_domain: QA / RAG / tool-use: corpus-level reasoning and information aggregation (GlobalQA: TopK/Count/Sort/MinMax) plus multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA).
problem_setting: Offline-trained, single-agent LLM that operates interactively at inference: the model interleaves reasoning with calls to four retrieval tools over a static document corpus until it has gathered sufficient evidence, then produces a final answer. Supervision is available via query-answer pairs (with gold supporting-document IDs) used to build expert trajectories (SFT) and to define rewards (RL). The central problem framing is that a single retriever with fixed top-k is a bottleneck for corpus-level (global) reasoning that requires complete document coverage and aggregation.
what_is_retrieved: Documents (corpus passages/documents) retrieved/operated on via four tools: semantic search, keyword search, document filtering (metadata/logical constraints), and aggregation (statistical/structural operations such as count, rank, set union/min/max). The retrieved unit is documents/document-IDs.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (the model retrieves from a fixed document collection via specialized tools; no agent-written growing memory).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness-oriented: explicitly targets recovery of the complete minimal set of supporting documents for corpus-level synthesis, moving beyond fixed top-k. A document-coverage reward R_E = F1(D_pred, D*) over document IDs rewards retrieving all necessary documents while minimizing irrelevant ones; evaluated with Document F1@k (D-F1@20).
retrieval_unit: document (problem operates at the document / document-ID granularity); tools also expose tool-API actions (semantic search, keyword search, filter, aggregate) over those documents.
index_source: Static corpus, built offline; not online/test-time induced. The retrievable store is the fixed GlobalQA (and multi-hop QA) corpora; tool indices (dense embeddings via BGE, keyword index) are constructed over this static corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat document index accessed through multiple tool interfaces: a dense/semantic vector index (BGE embeddings), a keyword-matching index, plus a metadata/constraint filter and an aggregation operator over document sets. Not a graph or hierarchy (the paper explicitly contrasts with graph-based RAG which loses document-level identifiers).
retriever_type: Hybrid multi-tool: dense semantic retriever (BGE/Qwen3 embeddings), keyword/sparse-style matching retriever, a filter model (Qwen3-4B used as filtering model), and an aggregation operator; an LLM policy coordinates which tool to call (tool-as-action). The individual retrievers are off-the-shelf; the coordination is learned.
retriever_learning_signal: The underlying retrievers (BGE / Qwen3 embeddings) are off-the-shelf (none / not retraining). The TOOL-COORDINATION POLICY (the LLM deciding how/when to call each tool) is learned via two-stage training: SFT on GPT-4-generated expert trajectories (with rejection sampling) followed by reinforcement learning (RLOO) using a composite reward (answer F1 + document-coverage F1 + tool-exploration reward).
query_construction: Thought-conditioned, model-generated tool calls: at each step the model emits intermediate reasoning R_t and a tool invocation C_t (e.g., a semantic-search query, a keyword query, a filter constraint, or an aggregation operation over previously retrieved document sets); sub-queries are decomposed per subquery and combined via explicit set operations (Union, Min, etc.).
query_granularity: Step/state-level: queries/tool-calls are constructed iteratively at each reasoning step within a trajectory (multi-step, up to a max number of retrieval steps), rather than a single one-shot query at t=0.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / adaptive (learned router): the model autonomously decides at each step whether and which tool to invoke, interleaving reasoning and retrieval until sufficient evidence is gathered. The when/how is learned via SFT+RL (learned policy), not a fixed schedule.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated tool requests produced by the learned policy: the model itself emits a tool call as part of its generated trajectory. The tool-exploration reward (R_T) shapes how many calls to make (rewarding sufficient-but-not-excessive calls relative to the expert trajectory's call count), so the trigger is a learned, reward-shaped decision rather than token-confidence or a complexity classifier.
reranking: [uncertain] No explicit dedicated reranking stage is described. Within tools, individual retrievers return top-ranked documents (TopK=20), and the aggregation tool can perform ranking/set operations, but no cross-encoder or RRF reranker is reported.
retrieved_context_refinement: Filtering/selection via the Document Filter tool (metadata/logical-constraint filtering, Qwen3-4B as filtering model) and the Aggregation tool (set operations such as union, count, min/max to synthesize/condense evidence). The policy iteratively narrows and combines document sets; no separate compression/distillation module is reported.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation within an interleaved reasoning-retrieval trajectory: retrieved documents (D_t) are appended to the context after each tool call and used by the model to reason in subsequent steps and produce the final answer. The policy that selects/sequences tools is itself trained as a learning signal (RL reward).
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-and-reason inside a search loop: the agent autonomously plans, retrieves, and integrates over multiple steps (S_t = (R_t, C_t, D_t)), progressively gathering and consolidating evidence; no MCTS/tree search. Plan and retrieval are intertwined (agentic RAG) rather than plan-then-retrieve.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call within a rollout: each reasoning step produces one tool invocation followed by retrieved documents, interleaving thinking and retrieval step by step until the final answer.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw documents / document IDs injected into context (the method explicitly preserves document-level boundaries and identifiers, contrasting with graph methods that lose provenance). Aggregation produces structured set-operation outputs (e.g., the min document ID).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document-level evidence (and their IDs); not a distilled strategy, workflow, or skill. The contribution emphasizes preserving fine-grained factual/numerical detail and provenance versus graph abstractions.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Reward-shaped training: the document-coverage F1 reward (R_E) penalizes irrelevant retrievals (precision term) while rewarding recall, and the tool-exploration reward (R_T) penalizes redundant/excessive calls; the Document Filter narrows the search space. Appendix A reports stable performance beyond ~10 retrieval steps, attributed to RL helping balance retrieval depth with over-retrieval noise control. No explicit relevance-evaluator/self-reflection module.
memory_type: none (no persistent episodic/skill/workflow memory; retrieval is over a static corpus within a single episode).
write_back: false. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into a persistent memory; evidence is gathered per-query within a trajectory and discarded after answering.
online_growth: false. The retrievable store is a fixed static corpus; it does not grow during deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back to a memory store; only model parameters are updated during the offline SFT+RL training phase).
failure_experience_usage: [uncertain] No explicit storage/retrieval of failed/negative experiences. During training, rejection sampling filters out low-quality/redundant expert traces (success-biased SFT data), and RL uses the RLOO leave-one-out baseline comparing trajectory rewards within a batch (so lower-reward rollouts contribute relatively negative advantages), but the paper does not describe an explicit failure-memory or contrastive failure mechanism.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored-memory entries to mutate; not applicable since there is no growing memory store).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: true. Tool selection/sequencing (the retrieval policy) is a learned RL-optimized policy: SFT cold-start (MARAG-CS) then RLOO RL with a composite reward, rather than a fixed similarity top-k. The paper frames learning 'both how and when to use' the tools as the core contribution.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / no. Single-agent private policy; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: GlobalQA (four task types: TopK, Count, Sort, MinMax) for corpus-level reasoning; 2WikiMultiHopQA and HotpotQA for multi-hop generalization. Backbone models: Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B-Instruct; retriever BGE; filter model Qwen3-4B; TopK=20.
benchmark_family: QA / corpus-level aggregation (GlobalQA, from the GraphRAG line) + multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA).
baselines: StandardRAG (single-round retrieval, Lewis et al. 2021), ITER-RETGEN (Shao et al. 2023), IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2023), HyperGraphRAG (Luo et al. 2025), Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025), ReCall (Chen et al. 2025; same multi-tool suite but optimized with answer-level reward only). Internal variants: MARAG (prompt-only, untrained multi-tool), MARAG-CS (SFT-only cold start), MARAG-R1 (SFT+RL).
key_metrics: F1 (token-level answer accuracy) and Document F1@k / D-F1@20 (document-coverage/execution F1 between retrieved and gold document sets at k=20). For multi-hop QA: EM and F1. Average number of tool calls reported as an efficiency/behavior metric.
headline_result: On GlobalQA with Qwen2.5-14B, MARAG-R1 achieves average F1 31.22 and D-F1@20 42.11, the best across all baselines and the SFT-only MARAG-CS (28.92 / 39.83); consistent SOTA across 3B (26.40 F1 / 37.05 D-F1@20) and 7B (28.60 / 38.44). ReCall (same tool suite, answer-only reward) scales only from 6.41 to 14.25 avg F1 (3B->14B) vs MARAG-R1's 26.40->31.22.
ablations: (1) Reward/stage ablation (Qwen2.5-14B, Table 2): w/o SFT 14.25 F1 / 20.00 D-F1@20 (largest drop, -17.0 F1 / -22.1 D-F1@20); w/o Answer Reward 13.78 / 24.48 (-17.4 F1 / -17.6 D-F1@20); w/o Document Reward 28.87 / 39.53 (-2.4 / -2.6); w/o Tool-Calls Reward 29.45 / 39.54 (-1.8 / -2.6) vs Full 31.22 / 42.11. (2) Tool ablation (Qwen2.5-7B, Table 4, Full 27.35/38.19): w/o Aggregation 10.48/19.54 (largest, -16.9 F1/-18.7 D-F1); w/o Keyword 13.03/24.08 (-14.3/-14.1); w/o Semantic 20.21/25.13 (-7.1/-13.1); w/o Document Filter 22.57/32.14 (-4.8/-6.0). (3) Tool-call count (Table 3): MARAG-R1 6.32 calls, MARAG-CS 6.27, ReCall 4.53, MARAG 2.81. (4) Appendix: retriever-scale (Qwen3 0.6B->8B: 31.22/42.11 -> 32.31/43.06) and filter-scale (Qwen3-4B->14B: 31.22 -> 31.82 F1) show graceful scaling; retrieval-step analysis shows stable performance beyond ~10 steps.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes (partially): document-level coverage (D-F1@20, an intrinsic retrieval/coverage metric over document IDs) is reported separately from token-level answer F1 (end-task), and average tool-call counts are reported separately. However, both are produced end-to-end by the same agent rather than via a decoupled retriever-only evaluation.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both: outcome (answer F1, EM) plus process/intermediate metrics — D-F1@20 (document-coverage/execution F1, treated as correctness of intermediate reasoning steps), average tool-call count, and training-dynamics analysis (training entropy/reward vs test F1/D-F1@20 correlation). Reward design itself includes process-level terms (document-coverage and tool-exploration rewards).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reports average tool calls per query as the main cost proxy: MARAG-R1 6.32 calls (vs MARAG-CS 6.27, ReCall 4.53, MARAG 2.81); the tool-exploration reward explicitly penalizes excessive calls to balance exploration with efficiency, and Appendix A shows performance saturating beyond ~10 retrieval steps (robust to over-retrieval). RL uses 5 sampled rollouts per query (RLOO). No wall-clock latency, token, or dollar-cost numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed per-tool TopK=20 for retrieval; D-F1 evaluated at k=20 (D-F1@20). The number of documents in context grows with the number of tool calls (effectively budget-capped by the max retrieval-step setting); k per call is fixed rather than adaptive. No explicit token-budget cap reported.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper). Uses existing GlobalQA (TopK/Count/Sort/MinMax, from the GraphRAG line), 2WikiMultiHopQA, and HotpotQA; specific train/test set sizes are not detailed in the paper text.
builds_on: RLOO / REINFORCE-style RL (Ahmadian et al. 2024); RL-for-retrieval agents Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025) and ReSearch/ReCall (Chen et al. 2025); agentic ReAct (Yao et al. 2023); GlobalQA benchmark from GraphRAG (Edge et al. 2025); BGE embeddings (Xiao et al. 2023); Qwen2.5/Qwen3 backbones; chunk-free/landmark-embedding retrieval (Luo et al. 2024); SFT cold-start from GPT-4 expert trajectories. Shares first-author lineage with R3-RAG (Li/Luo et al. 2025).
contrasts_with: Single-retriever fixed-top-k Workflow RAG (StandardRAG, ITER-RETGEN, IRCoT); graph-based RAG (GraphRAG, HyperGraphRAG, HippoRAG, KG-RAG — criticized for losing document-level provenance/identifiers); RL-RAG methods optimized with answer-only sparse reward (Search-R1, ReCall) — MARAG-R1 adds process-level rewards (document-coverage + tool-exploration) and a multi-tool suite.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task solving): agentic / reinforcement-learned RAG. Extends RL-trained iterative-retrieval agents (Search-R1, ReCall, ReSearch, R3-RAG) by coordinating MULTIPLE complementary retrieval tools (semantic/keyword/filter/aggregate) via SFT+RL with process-level rewards, explicitly targeting corpus-level/global retrieval and aggregation rather than local top-k multi-hop QA.
explicit_cbr_grounding: false. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
tool_document_engineering: [uncertain] Tools are described by their function (semantic/keyword/filter/aggregate) and the model learns usage via GPT-4 expert trajectories + SFT/RL; no explicit tool-description engineering (synthetic-query augmentation / weighted-field tool embeddings) is described.
index_content_separation: [uncertain] Not explicitly described; the four tools operate over the same static corpus and no progressive index-then-content disclosure scheme is reported.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index (fixed offline corpus and tools); tools are invoked via the model's generated tool calls (function-calling-style interleaved actions), not via a live external protocol such as RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP. No CRUD auto-sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial/implicit: tools are chained so that outputs of one feed another (e.g., Union of semantic+keyword search results, then Aggregation/Min over the combined set), and the learned policy sequences them; but there is no explicit inter-tool dependency graph or dependency-aware reranking.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no retrieved-case adaptation; this is not CBR). The closest analog is RL-reuse-finetuning of the tool-coordination policy.
